 Choi Hye-jin Grabs First-Round Lead with 9-Under at LPGA The Annika, Renewing Quest for Maiden Title
 Yu Byeongmin 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.13 09:11 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ Choi Hye-jin during the first round 
 Choi Hye-jin put on a stellar performance in the opening round of the LPGA Tour's The Annika driven by Gainbridge at Pelican (total purse $3.25 million), reigniting her quest for her first career victory. 
 Playing at the Pelican Golf Club (par 70) in Belleair, Florida, on the 13th (Korean time), Choi carded a bogey-free 9-under 61 with nine birdies, tying with Minami Katsu of Japan for the lead. 
 Choi, who made her LPGA Tour debut in 2022 and is still searching for her first win, has recently displayed form that brings her closer to the top of the leaderboard. 
 During the Asian swing, she finished as the runner-up consecutively at the Buick LPGA Shanghai in China and the BMW Ladies Championship in Haenam, South Korea, followed by a tied-ninth finish at the Maybank Championship held in Malaysia late last month. 
 Returning to the United States for The Annika, she maintained her sharp form, reopening the possibility of claiming her maiden LPGA Tour title. 
 Starting her round on the 1st hole (par 4), Choi picked up four birdies on the front nine starting from the 2nd hole (par 4). On the back nine, she reeled off four straight birdies from holes 12 to 15 and picked up another stroke on the final 18th hole (par 4) to cap off a flawless day. 
 On this day, Choi showcased pinpoint accuracy, missing the fairway only twice and the green just once, while needing 27 putts. 
 "I have been playing good rounds consistently lately, and I was able to finish well today with no major mistakes. I am very satisfied with playing a bogey-free round," Choi said. "I've been starting strongly in recent tournaments, and I have a good start once again. I will look to keep this going over the remaining three rounds." 
 Lindy Duncan of the United States shot an 8-under 62 to sit in third place, one stroke behind the co-leaders, highlighted by a hole-in-one on the 163-yard par-3 3rd hole using a 6-iron. 
 Aside from Duncan, Ally Corpuz of the United States also recorded a hole-in-one on the same hole using a 6-iron during the first round. 
 Corpuz finished the day tied for 31st at 3-under 67. 
 World No. 1 Nelly Korda of the United States, a three-time champion of this tournament, played her first event in two months by carding seven birdies without a bogey to start in fourth place at 7-under 63. 
 Yoon Ina finished the first round tied for 5th at 6-under 64; Kim A-lim, Lee Jeong-eun, and Kang Min-ji tied for 20th at 4-under 66; Yoo Hae-ran and Ko Jin-young tied for 31st; and Kim Sei-young and Im Jin-hee tied for 42nd at 2-under 68.
